summary: This is a fragment of a Maven pom.xml file, not Java code. It declares Mockito as a project dependency so tests can create stand-in "mock" objects for collaborators such as the TemperatureSensor interface instead of relying on real hardware.

lines.text: The <dependencies> block is where a Maven project lists every external library it needs; Maven downloads each one and puts it on the compile or test classpath for you.
An XML comment marking the spot where the JUnit 5 dependency already sits, so you can see the new entry is being added alongside it rather than replacing it.
Each library gets its own <dependency> element containing the coordinates Maven uses to locate the exact artifact.
The group id identifies the organization that publishes the library, which keeps names from colliding between different projects.
The artifact id names the specific library within that group; mockito-core is the mocking engine that provides mock() and when().
Pinning an exact version means everyone building the project gets identical behaviour instead of silently picking up a newer, possibly incompatible release.
Test scope makes Mockito available to test code only, so a mocking framework never ends up shipped inside your production build.
